title: Layered TAVRN over BLE proving ground
goal: Build and hardware-qualify a near-full proof-of-concept TAVRN-BLE testbed on micro:bit v2 using one shared BLE foundation and one TAVRN router whose base feature level is naive AODV, while preserving the proven controlled-flood fallback and adding TAVRN capabilities incrementally with TDD, reversible build flags, explicit deviations, and reproducible hardware evidence.
scope: Freeze a versioned TAVRN-BLE subset profile from TAVRN_v2.md, actual ns-3 behavior, the paper, and BLE constraints
Preserve the existing controlled-flood BLE node as the simple fallback while sharing safe radio/scheduler primitives

Improve the routed BLE link with explicit hop identity, logical next-hop addressing, custody ACK, bounded retry, failure events, controlled discovery flooding, tunable timing profiles, and reproducible manifests
Implement a single TAVRN router codebase that always contains the AODV route engine; first prove it with TAVRN_FEATURE_LEVEL=AODV_ONLY, then enable TAVRN extensions without replacing the route core

Add passive GTT, Smart TTL, fixed-k=1 ESC, mentorship/bootstrap, adaptive maintenance, TC-UPDATE, bounded verification, conditional metadata where the 24-byte budget permits, and medium-correctness local repair
Keep legacy flood and both TAVRN feature levels independently buildable/testable after every later slice
Integrate patient-beacon observations without changing fall/shout algorithms and quantify routing impact on beacon RX
Qualify direct, forced-relay, alternate transit-path recovery, multi-node, and finite overnight behavior with timestamped logs and exact source/artifact/board provenance
nonGoals: No production readiness, certification, clinical-readiness, or Bluetooth Mesh Protocol compliance claim
No cryptography, provisioning security, replay protection, persistent sequence state, secure boot, or adversarial-route defense in this proof of concept
No dynamic entropy k, mixed address widths, full ESC ambiguity recovery, IPv4/IPv6 port, or general MANET interoperability in this workplan
No third independent routing plugin: AODV_ONLY and FULL_TAVRN are feature levels of the same TAVRN router
No production power optimization, OTA update, NVM route persistence, polished CLI, dashboard rewrite, or deployment automation
No changes to patient fall/shout detection algorithms
No obligation to resolve checker nits, stylistic preferences, or production-only hardening findings that do not affect medium PoC correctness, hardware safety, layer boundaries, or acceptance
constraints: Branch is exp/tavrn-ble, based on the hardware-proven but currently uncommitted test/ble-bidi-pingpong work

Correctness target is medium: deterministic fixed capacity, bounds checking, serial-number/timer wrap policy, duplicate safety, loop prevention, route freshness, queue/failure handling, and reproducible tests; not production completeness

Test-driven development is auditable: each slice has a test-author step that records an exact red command with at least one assertion-level failure for new requirement IDs while all lower-profile suites stay green, followed by a separate implementation step and independent checker/re-check

Architecture has only two behavioral branches above shared BLE primitives: legacy controlled flooding and the TAVRN routed node. The TAVRN routed node always composes the same AODV engine; FULL_TAVRN adds modules and never replaces that engine

Build-time TRON_NODE_MODE={LEGACY_FLOOD,TAVRN_ROUTED}; TAVRN_FEATURE_LEVEL={AODV_ONLY,FULL_TAVRN} applies only to TAVRN_ROUTED; TRON_TIMER_PROFILE={FAST_TEST,BALANCED,SOAK}; optional test hooks are manifest-recorded

The legacy flood wire-v1 behavior and target remain buildable and golden-vector compatible. Shared radio/scheduler correctness fixes are allowed only with legacy regression proof; routed AODV/TAVRN use one shared wire-v2
The Phase 0 in-workspace TAVRN-BLE profile becomes sole firmware authority. It must resolve spec/source/paper conflicts and register all deviations

Fixed ESC k=1 is enabled only after AODV_ONLY hardware proof; canonical full identity is the six-byte AdvA/FICR BLE address, pre-ESC routed ID is a specified 16-bit suffix, fixed-k TAVRN ID is the specified low suffix byte, and collision handling fails closed; dynamic k is roadmap-only

Legacy advertising remains ADV_NONCONN_IND with at most 24 custom manufacturer bytes. Every type has a byte-offset budget, compile-time size guard, golden vector, dedupe key, and malformed-frame policy before implementation
Patient and TAVRN advertisements share RX windows on one nRF52833 radio; never claim simultaneous TX/RX
Firmware uses fixed-size structures and no heap in radio/link/routing/GTT/mentorship paths

Checker policy: resolve evidence-backed blocker/major findings affecting PoC correctness, hardware safety, acceptance, provenance, or architecture; explicitly defer/reject pedantic minor and production-polish findings

Commit sequence: commit the validated workplan alone; during execution inventory dirty foundation files, commit foundation source/tests separately, then for every slice obtain green tests/builds and checker acceptance, create an immutable clean candidate commit, build/flash that commit, and commit evidence separately. Never amend an already hardware-tested candidate

Hardware permission is blanket-approved by the user. Before every operation still verify normal micro:bit v2 mode, exact pyOCD UID, source commit/tree, submodule state, role/profile/timers/test hooks, ELF SHA-256, and serial link; flash one UID at a time and preserve logs
Three-board forced-relay AODV hardware proof is a mandatory gate before any TAVRN feature implementation; four-board local-repair topology must place repair at a transit node

After the completed BLE foundation/link work, `microbit/app/drivers/ble_radio.{c,h}` and `microbit/app/protocol/ble_mesh_scheduler.{c,h}` are frozen infrastructure for all remaining Phase 5, Phase 6, and final-classifier work. Classifiers and application/TAVRN semantics consume copied scheduler RX events above this boundary. Any driver/scheduler edit requires a separately approved hardware-defect exception, focused radio/scheduler regression, and legacy compatibility proof.

steps.title: Run attributable six-board AODV_ONLY versus TAVRN-BLE-V2.3 comparison
steps.target: six connected micro:bit v2 boards: 1=A, 2=B, 3=C, 4=D, 5=E, 6=F; physical layout A above B, B-E-F-C clustered left-to-right, D distant right
steps.action: Run continuous, user-stopped, six-board captures with optional compile-time CONTROL observability. Only A originates: one application-level-unacknowledged heartbeat per second continuously (normal hop-by-hop custody remains), plus a 10 Hz throughput stream for 60 seconds starting at t=60 s and recurring at 60+450k s. A→C uses reciprocal logical direct-RX blocking; B/D/E/F are relay candidates. Emit 1 s clock/application records and 10 s GTT/control-plane/counter/telemetry-health samples. One KISS Python controller owns six absolute-time captures, live watch, on-demand PNG snapshots, Ctrl-C finalization, hashes, and offline replay. Compare paired BALANCED AODV_ONLY and FULL_TAVRN repair-on captures with identical layout/workload; run repair-off control separately.
steps.validation: Live and final outputs report heartbeat offered/accepted/delivered PDR and p50/p95/p99 latency, per-burst throughput/goodput/PDR/latency, first delivery and route discovery, GTT precision/recall/Jaccard/staleness/churn against the known six-node truth set, per-type control messages/bytes and discovery/maintenance/verification/repair activity, scheduler TX/RX/channel-event proxies, retries/backpressure/faults, and telemetry health. Exact energy, PHY airtime/bytes, and radio wake-duration claims are excluded. Every accepted window has valid clock fits, no required-record drop/gap, exact artifact/UID/AdvA/profile/topology provenance, measured UART use below 50% per board, and raw logs retained even on protocol failure.

steps.title: Run available-board controlled test and finite overnight soak
steps.target: every qualified micro:bit v2 board physically available at execution

Make no scale claim beyond observed N and require the four-board repair gate separately.
steps.validation: Finite soak completes with active-set convergence, bounded recovery, explicit delivery denominator and zero unexplained reset/stall/corruption; all claims state exact N. Patient events are not required.

reviewFindings.title: Proof-of-concept scope governs checker triage
reviewFindings.detail: Resolve checker blocker/major findings tied to medium correctness, hardware safety, architecture, provenance, or acceptance. Explicitly defer/reject production security, certification, style, and polish requests outside scope.

reviewFindings.title: Blanket hardware authorization recorded
reviewFindings.detail: Repeated UID-targeted mass erase/load/reset and finite serial capture are approved. Exact target/artifact/UID/provenance checks remain mandatory.

reviewFindings.title: Profile model conflated legacy flood and link-v2
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in revision: retain legacy flood branch and one TAVRN routed implementation; AODV_ONLY/FULL_TAVRN are feature levels of the same router and share wire-v2.

reviewFindings.title: Hardware candidate provenance and commit order were circular
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in revision: clean immutable candidate commit precedes hardware; evidence is committed afterward; historical dirty-source logs are marked provenance-limited and baseline is re-proven.

reviewFindings.title: Four-board topology did not exercise transit local repair
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in revision: primary A-B-C with B as transit repairer and B-D-C alternate; suppress B-to-C custody ACKs.

reviewFindings.title: Wire, ACK, and identity contracts must freeze before implementation
reviewFindings.detail: Phase 0 now requires byte-level wire, custody ACK, full identity/suffix, frame capacity, dedupe, failure-event, and golden-vector contracts before link code.

reviewFindings.title: TAVRN mechanisms were ordered before their dependencies
reviewFindings.detail: Revision limits early GTT phase to passive state/Smart TTL, then fixed ESC/mentorship, then HELLO/metadata/expiry/verification, and finally local repair.

reviewFindings.title: Serial-number wrap/reboot policy required
reviewFindings.detail: Added to normative contract and AODV/GTT test requirements.

reviewFindings.title: Patient AdvA identity was discarded by scheduler event
reviewFindings.detail: Patient phase now first preserves/tests AdvA, vendors a hash-identified schema contract, defines exact classification/dedupe/sink/heartbeat policy, and uses emitted denominators.

reviewFindings.title: Final claims were written after final checker
reviewFindings.detail: Final checker moved after conformance/runbook generation and before final audit.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 1 link harness was mislabeled AODV_ONLY
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in JSON and Markdown: Phase 1 uses a dedicated non-routing link-v2 harness; AODV_ONLY is introduced only with the real AODV engine in Phase 2.

reviewFindings.title: TTL width and expanding-ring dedupe conflict
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: the PoC net diameter is 15, all traversal-derived timers were recomputed, and every expanding-ring transmission receives a fresh RREQ ID correlated only in local discovery state.

reviewFindings.title: Custody ACK occurs before router/application reservation
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: link-v2 uses synchronous two-phase candidate admission; ACCEPTED commits dedupe and HACK only after route/application storage reservation, with bounded BUSY cleanup and continued timer/control progress.

reviewFindings.title: Pre-ESC identity and reboot/dedupe semantics conflict
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: SID16 is the AdvA-derived standalone AODV_ONLY logical namespace, direct peers retain full AdvA, routed-common boot nonce handles incarnation, and equality dedupe is distinct from half-range freshness.

reviewFindings.title: Scheduler/link seams incomplete for AdvA and terminal outcomes
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: full AdvA/raw/RSSI seams, complete Phase-1 codec/link APIs, bounded radio and scheduler service, partial-channel accounting, and six typed ownership outcomes are frozen and checker-accepted.
reviewFindings.source: code-checker ses_03223af62ffexcEZVBNT8ZC0C6 findings 7-9 and final rechecks

reviewFindings.title: Timer, repair, and bounded-state registry incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: profile and architecture share the exact 71-key registry; repair uses one Smart-TTL plus one full attempt through deferred RERR; capacities, segmentation, and finite scheduler/radio bounds are explicit.

reviewFindings.title: Golden-vector and E_RREP_ACK correlation coverage incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: maximum-capacity and rejection vectors pass byte arithmetic, and E_RREP_ACK exact correlation includes destination sequence.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 0 specFiles and Markdown execution state stale
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: all seven Phase 0 contracts are registered, JSON/Markdown execution state is synchronized, and workplan validation passes.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 1 generated HACK receiver is reversed
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: generated HACK immediate_receiver is the prior DATA transmitter, and two independent link instances verify ACCEPTED, DUPLICATE, BUSY, and REJECTED correlation end to end.

reviewFindings.title: Legacy shared scheduler bypasses typed radio seams
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: legacy mesh scheduling now uses only bounded typed radio calls, stores/passes canonical AdvA, emits truthful typed TX outcomes, preserves causal masks across partial and restore faults, and fail-stops visibly.

reviewFindings.title: Dedicated Phase 1 firmware and provenance integration absent
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: the non-routing production-radio ble_link_v2_testbed, target-scoped generated profiles, strict identity inventory, runtime evidence, and durable artifact publisher are implemented and final-checker accepted.

reviewFindings.title: Full DATA and FLOOD caches lack deterministic replacement
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: DATA skips pinned entries and replaces the wrap-safe oldest legal victim with stable ties; FLOOD uses expired-first deterministic oldest replacement. Full, tie, wrap, and all-pinned tests pass.

reviewFindings.title: HELLO Q validation and wire guard coverage incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Explicitly deferred to targeted freshness/final maintenance acceptance. Partially resolved: illegal HELLO Q combinations are rejected and mandatory Section 11 capacity vectors/mutations pass. Nonblocking completeness remains for constant-based HACK16/HACK8/RREQ16/RREP16 guards and the HELLO16 bootstrap vector.

reviewFindings.title: Link harness cross-task queues are data-racy
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with fixed-capacity state protected by short μT-Kernel dispatch-disabled critical sections and host-tested reserve/ring behavior.

reviewFindings.title: Final-delivery reservation publishes before resolve
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: delivery remains provisional and invisible until ACCEPTED resolution succeeds; failure cancels without false delivery or leaked capacity.

reviewFindings.title: Harness service loop violates manifested poll bound
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: healthy cycles gate before poll, service one transition/dispatch, use a preemptible bounded wait, and inject/fail-stop before radio work on POLL_OVERRUN.

reviewFindings.title: Harness HACK suppression is not exact-current correlation
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved under the user-approved testbed adapter: pre-call ordinal/state capture plus full decoded tuple/status/full-AdvA matching removes only the exact newly generated HACK and covers duplicate handling.

reviewFindings.title: Harness final-application policy is too permissive
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: only the exact diagnostic application shape is accepted; permanent rejection precedes transient BUSY and unsupported input consumes no BUSY hook.

reviewFindings.title: Generated timer registry is not runtime authority
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: one immutable generated tron_timer_config_t governs implemented scheduler, queue, link-harness, and legacy timing consumers; host tests link the frozen profile object.

reviewFindings.title: Global CMake inputs contaminate legacy target
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: explicit Phase 1 target selection scopes validation/builds, cross-target inputs fail configure, and the effective legacy hook alias is compiled and tested.

reviewFindings.title: Candidate inventory omits selected-width fleet collision checks
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: every TSV AdvA is semantically parsed, SID16 uniqueness/nonreservation gates Phase 1, and SID8/full-identity status plus selected record/hash are manifested.

reviewFindings.title: Artifact manifest and candidate eligibility are incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: complete capacity/timer/source/tool/identity/hook/eligibility schema and durable exact build-command/config sidecars are published with sizes and SHA-256 values.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime evidence cannot prove Phase 1 hardware acceptance
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: parseable identity equality, effective timer/hook configuration, causal outcomes/faults, hook activation, delivery, and transaction summary records support the planned two-board proof.

reviewFindings.title: SID16-only Phase 1 rejects reserved SID8 unnecessarily
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: Phase 1 eligibility gates SID16 only while SID8 reservation/uniqueness is derived and manifested for future fixed-k activation.

reviewFindings.title: Build tests miss acceptance-critical harness behavior
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved for Step 1b with queue/reservation/policy/HACK/poll-gate tests, target contamination and fleet fixtures, exact manifest/sidecar checks, and dirty-candidate rejection. Positive clean candidate publication belongs to Step 1c after the immutable commit.

reviewFindings.title: Ordinary logger output deterministically trips poll bound
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: logger is lower priority, mesh uses a bounded preemptible wait, and the wrap-safe pre-poll gate skips radio work and fails closed before an over-budget poll.

reviewFindings.title: Effective build command evidence is hashed then deleted
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: exact selected-target Ninja commands, compile_commands, build.ninja, CMake cache, and generated config sidecars survive publication and are named/hashed/sized in the final manifest.

reviewFindings.title: Immediate HACK eligibility races the sender's three-channel TX burst
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by DEV-023: every centralized receiver-side HACK producer uses validated hack_turnaround_ms sourced from the existing 8 ms radio TX-event bound and post-poll observation time. Assertion-level RED/green, wrap, all-producer, build, and adversarial checks passed. Immutable candidate 4afe720 then completed 100/100 unhooked custody transfers with balanced channel evidence and passed controlled HACK-drop/BUSY benches.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 3 router drops terminal DATA ownership
reviewFindings.detail: Router ignores/rejects ownership-bearing terminal link events and can return BUSY before consuming a synchronous LOCAL_TX_NOT_ATTEMPTED outcome; transit dedupe custody can remain pinned and immutable DATA context is lost.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 3 router ACKs DATA without durable exact reservation
reviewFindings.detail: Router mutates AODV before resolving candidate, lacks a final-delivery reservation seam, and does not validate the supplied event against link's current immutable candidate or roll back failed resolution.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 3 router loses backpressured link failure
reviewFindings.detail: AODV_FAILURE_BUSY from RETRY_EXHAUSTED is returned without retaining the failed next hop for retry.

reviewFindings.title: Phase 3 duplicate and max-hop evidence is unreachable
reviewFindings.detail: Committed duplicate DATA/FLOOD cannot emit passive evidence, and hop-15 semantic subjects suppress valid one-hop direct-transmitter evidence.

reviewFindings.title: Router extraction lacks complete action dispatch and delivery commit
reviewFindings.detail: Final-delivery reserve/cancel alone is insufficient: router common must own retained AODV action dispatch and commit exact application reservations for both feature levels.

reviewFindings.title: Single pending failure slot lacks overlap capacity proof
reviewFindings.detail: RERR backpressure can outlast one retry episode; retain/coalesce all overlapping failed peers in bounded router state and test two distinct failures.

reviewFindings.title: Router must use public candidate-match seam
reviewFindings.detail: Add a narrow link-owned fieldwise candidate-match API; router must not inspect mutable link candidate internals directly.

reviewFindings.title: Common terminal consumer must cover every link output API
reviewFindings.detail: Candidate resolve, scheduler, tick, dispatch, and all sends can return ownership events; router common must consume each before interpreting primary status and treat failed transit release as an invariant fault.

reviewFindings.title: AODV transit hops 15 must not overflow
reviewFindings.detail: Shared read-only DATA admission/commit validation must reject forwarding encoded hops=15 while still allowing local delivery and direct-only passive evidence.

reviewFindings.title: Router extraction capacities and manifests remain incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Document and manifest router retained action, accepted-DATA reservation, delivery reservation, and pending-failure capacities while completing original Step 3b profile integration.

reviewFindings.title: Router failure obligations can be lost or overtaken
reviewFindings.detail: Failure retry occurs after AODV tick, new obligations can overtake retained ones, and capacity four can overflow after link custody is freed. Use route-capacity ordered/coalesced storage and process oldest before other AODV mutation.

reviewFindings.title: Application reservation state lacks cancel/fault lifecycle
reviewFindings.detail: Cancel clears reservation before successful cancellation; commit INVALID creates an implicit permanent deadlock. Model explicit reserved/cancel-pending/post-ACK states and a visible fail-stop disposition.

reviewFindings.title: Permanent tracked-control send leaks ACK-wait token
reviewFindings.detail: Router clears a permanently failed tracked RREP without marking sent or cancelling the unsent token, exhausting the four ACK-wait reservations.

reviewFindings.title: Decoded unadmitted DATA/FLOOD returns router OK
reviewFindings.detail: Scheduler handler returns OK merely on decode for wrong-next-hop, mesh-faulted, or capacity-rejected traffic without committed counter evidence.

reviewFindings.title: Pending failure and blacklist router events lose typed context
reviewFindings.detail: Router collapses AODV pending-data failure and blacklist actions into a generic counter/IGNORED, preventing routed main from preserving distinct destination/peer behavior.

reviewFindings.title: Failure queue still lacks fail-safe overflow and global gating
reviewFindings.detail: Capacity 16 alone does not stop new AODV/link work from producing a 17th peer; overflow currently releases transit custody and loses the break obligation. Gate mutation/promotion on oldest failure and preserve/fail-stop any overflow event.

reviewFindings.title: Reserve-token and delivery mismatch invariants are not latched
reviewFindings.detail: reserve OK with token zero and delivery/action mismatch return INVALID without typed fail-stop, allowing reservation leakage or repeated deadlock.

reviewFindings.title: Post-ACK AODV ingest invariant lacks typed fail-stop
reviewFindings.detail: Non-BUSY post-ACK ingest failures retain DATA but leave router usable, causing repeated mutation attempts indefinitely.

reviewFindings.title: Untyped dispatch compatibility wrapper discards events
reviewFindings.detail: Legacy tavrn_router_dispatch wrapper silently drops pending-data/blacklist context produced by dispatch_ex.

reviewFindings.title: Transit release invariant must latch fail-stop
reviewFindings.detail: Failed required dedupe release increments a counter but leaves router usable despite unresolved ownership state.

reviewFindings.title: Incomplete FULL relay trips scheduler poll fail-stop under long forced-relay traffic
reviewFindings.detail: In the matched 625 s BALANCED FULL_TAVRN_PHASE3 smoke, relay B latched scheduler_fault=1 and mesh_fault=1 at about 440 s after 218 end-to-end deliveries. AODV_ONLY completed 300/300 under the same topology/settings. Causality is not yet established; reproduce with exact cycle-phase/elapsed telemetry before correction.

reviewFindings.title: Routed local_fault telemetry is too coarse for smoke diagnosis
reviewFindings.detail: Destination C accumulated seven generic local_fault counts in AODV_ONLY and four in incomplete FULL while continuing delivery. Router fail-stop reason remained NONE, so current telemetry cannot distinguish normal rejected/ignored control paths from ownership/action invariant errors.

reviewFindings.title: FULL hardware observability lacks GTT snapshot and RREQ-scope telemetry
reviewFindings.detail: Current routed summaries expose delivery/link/AODV aggregate state but not deterministic GTT membership/freshness or per-ring initial/full scopes, so Phase 3 hardware can smoke the prefix but cannot prove passive membership or Smart-TTL fallback.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime RED lacks an executable production-cycle seam
reviewFindings.detail: The frozen API is only a passive stopwatch/record container; production main could retain independent phase ordering and still satisfy tests, so captured scheduler replay would not test the real cycle.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime timing contract misses startup and next-poll boundary
reviewFindings.detail: Contract combines poll/event handling, lacks initial RX-return seed and explicit next-poll-start check, and does not test equality-versus-strict overrun, invalid ordering or half-range ambiguity.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime diagnostics permit fabricated cross-source combinations
reviewFindings.detail: One unconstrained record stores scheduler/router/link/AODV payloads simultaneously while current router APIs hide consumed action/link outcomes. Freeze producer-owned phase-discriminated traces and expose truthful router trace seams.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime GTT RED fixture and snapshot semantics are invalid
reviewFindings.detail: Fixture AdvAs are not random-static and claimed freshness contradicts query/deadlines; contract does not freeze active-only versus all-retained completeness/self/tombstone behavior.

reviewFindings.title: RREQ telemetry RED is not production-backed
reviewFindings.detail: Hand-authored records do not prove fresh IDs/ring progression/Smart-TTL fallback or distinguish AODV action admission from later link admission.

reviewFindings.title: Runtime queue malformed/overflow and requirement mapping coverage is incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: open-deferred-unrelated: diagnostic overflow does not prove retained sentinels, RREQ overflow is absent, malformed/null/inconsistent states are untested, and several requirement labels cover only fabricated values. Remaining RREQ queue overflow coverage belongs to step-5f-rreq-verification or step-5h and does not block wire-free local expiry.

reviewFindings.title: Captured FULL relay overrun is voluntary-yield timer quantization, not router/FULL service order
reviewFindings.detail: Matched telemetry-enabled FULL_TAVRN hardware capture faulted passive relay B at 1577 ms. The scheduler returned at 1574 ms, all protocol phases consumed zero measured milliseconds, and HEALTHY_YIELD requested 1 ms but completed at 1577 ms. microT-Kernel relative delays add TIMER_PERIOD, so a one-millisecond tk_dly_tsk cannot satisfy the frozen two-millisecond return-to-next-poll bound. Step 5.3 was narrowed to this captured replay before any production correction.

reviewFindings.title: Scheduler correction must preserve logger liveness
reviewFindings.detail: The mesh task priority is higher than the logger task, so a correction that simply removes or skips every healthy yield would satisfy the poll bound while starving queued diagnostics. Step 5.4 now requires a finite virtual logger-sentinel dequeue with all scheduler-return gaps <=2 ms.

reviewFindings.title: LOGGER-LIVENESS-01 overstates progress when the cyclic release bit is already set
reviewFindings.detail: The production event flag is level-triggered and coalescing; tk_wai_flg returns immediately when the bit is already set, so the higher-priority mesh can consume releases without dispatching the logger. The virtual test currently dequeues on every callback and its poll-bound-1 negative control does not model admitted nonblocking waits. Fix with an actual logger progress epoch, stale-release-aware bounded waiting, and an admitted stale-bit negative control.

reviewFindings.title: Short scheduler-fix smoke exposes terminal router INVALID on leaf C
reviewFindings.detail: The matched 60-second smoke stopped at 751 ms on C. Timing remained healthy (scheduler gap 0 ms); phase SCHEDULER_EVENT returned TAVRN_ROUTER_EVENT_INVALID with no typed router terminal fault, then cycle fail-stop operated as designed. Leading hypothesis is routine broadcast overhearing of an AODV control addressed to another immediate receiver being classified INVALID rather than IGNORED; raw control type/receiver is not present in the retained trace, so reproduce in host before changing behavior.

reviewFindings.title: Repeated bootstrap TX_DONE can postpone AODV_ONLY establishment forever
reviewFindings.detail: Every repeated N=1 TX_DONE overwrites the establishment epoch while repeats are emitted every half-window; latch the first successful completion and cancel outstanding bootstrap work before N=0.

reviewFindings.title: BUSY incarnation reset deadlocks and a second peer can overwrite the pending slot
reviewFindings.detail: Global route bar prevents action dispatch from freeing reservation capacity, and pending ownership is checked too late. Reject any distinct second reset before mutation and permit safe unrelated draining while quarantining barred-peer work.

reviewFindings.title: Incarnation reset misses routes to peer and retains serial high-water
reviewFindings.detail: Reset selects only next-hop routes. It must also invalidate destination==peer and clear the rebooted destination freshness after constructing RERR so sequence 1 can be relearned.

reviewFindings.title: Incarnation reset leaves stale queued AODV/link/router work
reviewFindings.detail: Peer-owned queued actions, retained router action, anonymous HACK/relay work and flood dedupe can survive reset. Quarantine on BUSY and purge on commit without allowing pre-reset work to escape.

reviewFindings.title: Distinct AdvAs sharing SID16 are admitted ambiguously
reviewFindings.detail: Before direct N=1 admission, reject equal logical SID with different full AdvA, bar the ambiguous identity and invalidate affected route use fail-closed.

reviewFindings.title: REJOINING aliases BUSY and is not observable as a distinct typed status
reviewFindings.detail: Assign a unique router event value, extend routed-cycle validation, and test distinct BUSY versus REJOINING trace records.

reviewFindings.title: Application-cancel BUSY can delete already-reserved incarnation RERR
reviewFindings.detail: Retry reruns AODV reset, and peer-action purge can remove the first reserved RERR. Track an AODV-committed pending phase and preserve locally originated RERR segments.

reviewFindings.title: SID16 conflict does not prefilter compressed traffic from unrecorded colliding AdvA
reviewFindings.detail: Bar lookup by full AdvA misses the second colliding identity. Reject compressed DATA/control/FLOOD by barred logical SID before link admission while allowing full-identity bootstrap diagnostics.

reviewFindings.title: Relayed delivery reservation can survive origin incarnation reset
reviewFindings.detail: Delivery cancellation checks only immediate transmitter, not DATA origin/final identity, leaving singleton delivery state stranded after AODV action purge.

reviewFindings.title: Purged unsent RREP actions leak ACK-wait reservations
reviewFindings.detail: AODV action compaction and router retained-action purge discard nonzero action tokens without calling aodv_core_cancel_unsent_action, exhausting fixed ACK-wait slots over time.

reviewFindings.title: Retained RREP/RREP_ACK and sent ACK-wait state can survive incarnation reset
reviewFindings.detail: Router peer-action parsing covers only RREQ/RERR, so retained RREP/RREP_ACK naming the rebooted peer through another next hop can escape. Sent ACK waits are cleared only by expected peer, not destination/origin, and may later blacklist the wrong next hop.

reviewFindings.title: Link incarnation reset misses custody/candidate identity ownership and pinned dedupe release
reviewFindings.detail: Custody and candidate cleanup match only next hop/transmitter, while queued DATA matching also recognizes origin/final identity. READY/ACTIVE slots can survive or strand after queue removal, and transit dedupe pins are not released before slot reset, eventually exhausting fixed capacity.

reviewFindings.title: Transit DATA dedupe pin can survive reset before custody-slot creation
reviewFindings.detail: RX acceptance pins dedupe before router forwarding creates a link custody slot. If reset purges the retained/queued forward action in that interval, slot-based cleanup cannot release the pin; repeated resets can exhaust all fixed dedupe entries. Add action-level pin release or endpoint-aware pinned-dedupe cleanup and a regression covering the pre-custody interval.

reviewFindings.title: Freeze and prove mixed-width production bootstrap path
reviewFindings.detail: Existing wire/link/router seams reject SID16 bootstrap/SYNC once local width is SID8, so an established mentor cannot admit a late newcomer or recover context loss. Step 5.7/5.8 must cover production-composed mixed-width admission and atomic transitions.

reviewFindings.title: Freeze mentorship snapshot and compressed-context membership
reviewFindings.detail: Canonical snapshot must include self plus retained non-purged records and transfer departed tombstones; SID8 ambiguity must ignore departed records but include retained hard-expired non-departed records.

reviewFindings.title: Add bounded full-identity JOIN after both bootstrap paths
reviewFindings.detail: Self-bootstrap-only JOIN cannot converge independently bootstrapped nodes. Phase 4 needs bounded JOIN originate/admit/dedupe/merge/collision/relay after mentorship and self-bootstrap.

reviewFindings.title: Gated FULL dispatch returns invalid zero trace
reviewFindings.detail: Mentorship dispatch returns while gated without a valid DISPATCH trace; routed_cycle rejects the zero phase and enters fault-idle before bootstrap progresses.

reviewFindings.title: Production mentorship exchange is not driven
reviewFindings.detail: Firmware does not send due offers, select/send pulls, answer SYNC_PULL, send next pull, or activate from final page; tests currently call helpers directly.

reviewFindings.title: Mentorship session does not authorize exact complete snapshot
reviewFindings.detail: Unsolicited/reordered/mismatched pages can establish context and public activation does not require exact offered count/index/final completion.

reviewFindings.title: SID8 collision path does not fully fail closed
reviewFindings.detail: Direct outer AdvA mismatch can alias a unique SID8; JOIN collision does not gate compressed traffic, enter conflict, or invalidate incompatible state.

reviewFindings.title: JOIN queue backpressure loses convergence work
reviewFindings.detail: Origin/relay JOIN is attempted once; relay dedupe is committed before successful enqueue and no bounded retry retains queue-full work.
